producedBy: read-only deployment telemetry and SRE investigation
sanitization: Aggregate counts, bounded timing summaries, and build identities only; raw logs, request bodies, SQL, host/process identifiers, and personal data omitted.

providerMetricsCoverage.averageCpuMemory: low per aggregate provider metrics; exact values not retained
providerMetricsCoverage.limitations: Only two readiness requests were returned; these aggregates do not establish user-request impact, active instance count, or absence of unobserved load.

providerMetrics.limitations: Only three requests were returned and all observed endpoint samples were readiness probes; zero 5xx points do not prove zero user-facing failures. The instance-count series is inconsistent.

reportedIdleWindows.ownerObservation: The owner reports no noticed downtime during active use; noticed interruptions occur while the app is idle or unused.
reportedIdleWindows.correlationMethod: Read-only log and metric samples around ±5 minutes of each reported time; this is temporal correlation, not request-level tracing.

providerCoverage.limitations: Endpoint metrics contained readiness probes only, not ordinary-user traffic. Zero observed 5xx points do not establish that user requests succeeded.

reportedIdleWindows.historicalSearchDiscrepancy: An Oct 21 exact-window search returned no records; the Nov 2 unrevision-filtered ±5-minute query found samples around these anchors. The reader/window discrepancy remains unresolved.

serverJobFailureReview.queryScope: Read-only production replica; live scope; failed scheduled-evaluation jobs completed in the interval. Selected only static job type, status, error codes, attempt counts/outcomes, and timestamps; actor IDs, input payloads, result data, and raw error messages were not returned.

boundedErrorMessageClassification.method: A SQL CASE expression inspected error-message text but returned only coarse category labels; raw messages were not selected or returned.
boundedErrorMessageClassification.limitation: Text-token classification is heuristic. Generic handler_failed codes and unclassified messages do not rule out database, provider, or application causes.

sourceReview.executionPath: The handler iterates dates for a scope and wraps each date's runWebPushAlerts call in the protected commit boundary. That path performs database work and serial external push sends before the boundary returns.
sourceReview.risk: A protected per-date operation can keep its job-row transaction/lock open while database calls and external push delivery run. This is a plausible pool/worker-pressure contributor, not a proven cause of the observed degradation.
sourceReview.errorBoundary: Provider send exceptions are caught and recorded by delivery handling; generic handler_failed receipts do not identify whether an uncaught database, cancellation, or other application error triggered the retry.
sourceReview.nextValidation: Use a synthetic slow-send test with pool acquisition and lease timing to measure the protected boundary. Do not change the production job boundary solely from temporal correlation.

serverJobFailureReview.reconciliation: The narrower 04:17–04:21Z query found two distinct failed jobs with six attempt receipts. A query matching the readiness sample's five-minute window found three failed and one cancelled job on the production read replica, versus five terminal failures reported by readiness. The time/window or telemetry-versus-replica discrepancy remains unresolved.

counterScope.poolCounters: Process-local pool measurements, not an Autoscale fleet aggregate.
counterScope.instanceMapping: No retained instance identity is available to map the process to one Autoscale instance.

assessment.finding: Production telemetry around the owner-reported idle windows and two Nov 2 periods shows recurring process-local pool contention overlapping with background-job, queue-monitor, rollover, outbox, and push-enqueue failures.
assessment.confidence: High that pool contention and worker failures recurred; moderate that they align with low-traffic/idle periods; low that they caused the reported interruptions or identify the initiating cause.
assessment.causeBoundary: Aggregated telemetry does not identify whether slow database work, event-loop stalls, or another upstream condition initiated the pressure, and cannot correlate an individual failed user request. Readiness success after an incident does not prove uninterrupted service.

nextDiagnostic.action: Correlate primary-database query and connection waits, per-instance pool/event-loop samples, request outcomes, and the five terminal scheduled-job failure details for 2026-11-02 04:17–04:21 UTC before changing configuration or infrastructure.

assessment.finding: Read-only telemetry shows recurring short-lived application-side, process-local database-pool contention on the serving build, with pool saturation, queued checkouts, acquisition errors, event-loop delay, and database-timeout warnings.
assessment.confidence: High that pool contention recurred; low that it caused user-visible downtime or identifies the initiating mechanism.
assessment.causeBoundary: Available aggregate telemetry cannot determine whether event-loop stalls, slow database work, or another upstream condition initiated the pressure, and cannot assign request-level causality.
assessment.impactBoundary: Provider metrics returned only a few readiness requests in the sampled windows and cannot establish ordinary-user impact or prove there were no failures.

nextDiagnostic.action: Capture synchronized primary-database query/connection/lock waits, per-instance pool and event-loop intervals, request outcomes, and terminal-job failure details; first reconcile the Oct 21 versus Nov 2 historical log-query discrepancy.
